title: Producing a compiled résumé
summary: One POST /resumes/finalize: selection against the parsed job description, model assembly, a signed compile in the sealed build container, and the fit loop that recompiles until the document is one page.
note: Drawn for POST /api/v1/resumes/finalize, the only path that runs the whole chain; /resumes/model stops after assembly and /resumes/compile stops after the first compile. Nothing in this path calls a language model: the same graph, job description and template produce the same PDF byte for byte, because SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH is fixed from the target's created_at. Artifacts are skipped entirely when NODE_ENV is 'test' (resumes.ts:402), so a test run finalizes without touching object storage.

actors.label: Browser (Tailor)
actors.note: Sends the target id, template key, and any manual curation: pins, blocks, explicit atom order, per-section and per-item configuration.

actors.label: resumes router
actors.note: Orchestrates prepare → compile → fit → persist. All three of model, compile and finalize share the same prepare().

actors.label: resume service
actors.note: tailor(), renderTemplate(), compileResume(). The only layer that escapes text on its way into LaTeX.

actors.label: @vitae/core algorithms
actors.note: Pure functions: scoreAtoms, selectAtoms/selectManual, estimateLines, planFitStep, applyFitStep. Testable without a database.

actors.label: Postgres
actors.note: Atoms, variants, the graph, the target record, and where the finalized résumé and its artifacts land.

actors.label: buildsvc (Tectonic)
actors.note: A separate container. HMAC-gated, no runtime network, --untrusted, per-request temp directory.

actors.label: Object storage
actors.note: Cloudinary adapter. Holds the PDF and .tex bytes; the résumé record keeps only keys and hashes.

steps.label: POST /resumes/finalize { targetId, templateKey, pins, blocks, atomOrder, ... }
404 NOT_FOUND when the target does not exist
steps.note: prepare() also rejects a body that mixes curation modes before any work is done (assertCuratedBody, resumes.ts:60).

steps.label: load the target's parsed keywords, the template line model, and the graph once
steps.note: FR-102: one graph load serves both the static-section model and the final model. The job description was parsed into weighted keywords earlier, when the target was created.

steps.label: shrink the budget by the static sections, then tailor()
steps.note: Skills, education, awards, research and summary consume lines the knapsack does not know about, so a static model is built first and its measured lines subtracted from lines_per_page.

steps.label: scoreAtoms against the keywords, then selectAtoms within the line budget
steps.note: Auto mode is a budgeted greedy optimiser over saturating keyword coverage plus quality; manual mode takes `include` as the exact ordered list. Pinned atoms are forced in, blocked ones excluded.

steps.label: selection entries with per-atom emphasis and line counts
buildFullModel: group by owner, fold in skills, education, awards, contacts
steps.note: The model is scoped to the person node marked is_self. With no such anchor it produces an EMPTY model (resume-model.ts:477) rather than rendering the whole graph under a placeholder name. The graph holds other people's roles and degrees.

steps.label: renderTemplate: splice the model into main.tex, escaping every dynamic value
steps.note: Guillemet tokens are replaced one by one; assertNoUnresolvedTokens then throws rather than compiling a document with «SECTIONS» printed in it. Only the renderers may emit unescaped macros.

steps.label: POST /compile signed with HMAC over timestamp + '.' + raw body
steps.note: The signing key IS the authentication (FR-027). The service refuses to start with no secret, and refuses in production with any of the published development defaults.

steps.label: 401 BAD_SIGNATURE: missing header, >5min skew, or digest mismatch
tectonic --untrusted --only-cached in a fresh temp dir, then pdfinfo and pdftotext
steps.note: The package cache is warmed at image build time and the runtime network is sealed, so --only-cached makes a cache miss fail fast instead of hanging in DNS timeouts. The temp dir is removed in a finally block.

steps.label: { pdf (base64), pages, text }, or 400 COMPILE_ERROR with a guessed section and log tail
steps.note: A compile failure is a structured error, not a 500. If the service is unreachable at all, the client returns { offline: true } and the caller falls back to a .tex download (FR-RES-013).

steps.label: coverage: measure the parsed keywords against the extracted PDF text
steps.note: Measured from the output, not the model that produced it. That is what catches a keyword the selection intended to include but the template hyphenated or pushed off the page. The gate passes at 0.95 weighted.

steps.label: while pages > 1 and fewer than 3 iterations: planFitStep, applyFitStep, rebuild, recompile
steps.note: planFitStep at resumes.ts:330 chooses a concise-swap or a drop, never touching a pinned atom. If no step is available, or three iterations were not enough, needsManualTrim is set and the loop stops rather than dropping something the person pinned.

steps.label: upload the PDF and .tex bytes, keyed by SHA-256
steps.note: Wrapped in try/catch: a storage outage must not block finalize. The record is written with null keys and Outputs offers a re-export instead.

steps.label: one transaction: résumé record + attachments + revision (+ base pointer if first final)
steps.note: status is 'final' only when the compile succeeded, the document is exactly one page, and coverage passed the gate; otherwise 'draft'.

steps.label: { id, status, onePage, gatePassed, needsManualTrim, fitDecisions, coverage, pages }
steps.note: fitDecisions is the audit trail of what the loop trimmed and why, so a person can see what the one-page constraint cost them.
